posts.text:
"I started thinking about guns in America.” I talk to veteran London-based broadcaster @MishalHusain about being at the White House Correspondents' Dinner as shots were fired. “How fortunate we are to live in a country where that kind of threat is thankfully very remote,” she tells me.

Video

“A moment of stability and reassurance”: Veteran British broadcaster @MishalHusain says that, at a difficult time between Washington and London, King Charles managed to seize a complicated diplomatic moment.

Video

"I support Israel and we must continue to support Israel. But there was a slaughter of the Palestinian people in Gaza." On America's relationship with Israel @wendyrsherman tells me, "things have changed, I spend a lot of time with younger people. I try to listen and learn as my parents did with me during the Vietnam war... Israel must be safe and secure and have peace forever. And the Palestinians have to be able to have dignity and a place they can call their own as well."

Video

"I don't think they're fractured. I think they have a very clear sense of what has happened in this war." @vali_nasr gives his take on what Iranian leadership is thinking right now-- "They were willing to talk to President Trump. I think where there is a division is how to respond to his erratic behavior."

Video

"I think the Trump administration is in a very difficult place." @wendyrsherman says-- "I don't think [the blockade] will change the calculus of Iran. It's existential for them. For Donald Trump, it is political. It's markets. It's munitions. And it's the midterms... I believe Donald Trump believes he can sustain this and his other choices-- escalate even further, or declare victory and go away-- are not good choices."

Video

"Russia has turned all its economy into a war machine. It's extremely difficult to turn back." 
When we spoke in Prague, Czech President Petr Pavel warned how President Putin may push his luck in the Baltics, just to humiliate NATO.

Video

"We need to talk to each other as equals, not as a dependent child." 
Czech President Petr Pavel says President Trump needs a reality check about his EU allies. Speaking to me at a @CNNPrima conference in Prague, Pavel told me just what he thinks the US President needs to hear:

Video
Also Wolf’s agent, and what a great job of reporting he did that night.

Calm, collected and carrying on in a scary crisis, my super cool agent Michael Glantz‼️
So glad everyone made it safely out of that ballroom.

nytimes.com/2026/04/26/us/po…

Congratulations to the winners of the Goldman environmental prize! For the first time ever, all of its six winners are women activists. Each fighting for a greener, cleaner world.

Video

As Chinese interest in Iranian culture surges, from my archives, the unexpected tourism boom in the late 1990s. When tourists came to see ancient Persian landmarks despite concerns about visiting the usually closed-off country.

Video

An escape ten years in the making. In this report, @ValerioCNN follows the incredible journey of one North Korean family who made a desperate bid to reach South Korea and freedom.

Video

"We live in constant wars, endless wars, which we think lead to nowhere, with no exit strategy... no conflict was ever resolved by simply military means." Former Israeli diplomat and Knesset member, Colette Avital tells me she's "fighting to make Israel a normal country again."

Video

“I think there's probably a difference between what President Trump wants and what the administration as a whole wants.” Ricardo Zúniga, who led U.S. negotiations with Cuba under President Obama, sees a conflicting agenda in America’s current Cuba policy.

Video

“Both sides are playing a game of chicken right now.” Nate Swanson served as the National Security Council's Iran Director under both Presidents Biden and Trump. He tells me Iran and the U.S. are in a "test of wills," waiting to see who blinks first.

Video
Today’s @NYTGames Midi Crossword! So proud of this career milestone!! 😁

Historian @TimothyDSnyder sums up a year of Trump choices and policies in one overall conceptual framework, which he calls “Superpower suicide.”

Video

“As Americans, we have to be able to say it's not normal to wish for the destruction of an entire civilization.” Historian @TimothyDSnyder tells me why, when President Trump threatens to eradicate Iranian civilization, he "taints" all Americans by publicly using genocidal rhetoric.

Video

You can watch my full interview with President Zelensky @ZelenskyyUa here. We discussed the impact of the war in the Middle East and how he's navigating an increasingly complex relationship with the US. cnn.com/2026/04/22/tv/video/…
